candidates.title: Cadet/Graduate Engineer
candidates.abstract: Civil Design team, Major Projects is looking for an enthusiastic and motivated Cadet/Graduate Engineer to join our team
bullets: Cadet/Graduate Engineer Opportunity with Civil Design Team
Permanent full time opportunity/35 hours per week
Enjoy flexible work hours, EAP, skin checks, flu shots, supportive work culture
candidates.content_text:
Waverley Council is inviting applications for an enthusiastic and motivated Cadet/Graduate Engineer to join our Civil Design team, Major Projects. This is an exciting opportunity where you’ll gain hands-on experience delivering civil and infrastructure projects that make a real difference.
Why Join Us?
- Permanent full-time, 35 hours per week
- Salary - Cadet Engineer - $60,541.99 - $69,623.30 plus 12% Super; Graduate Engineer - $76,921.61 - $88,459.86 plus 12% Super
- Close to public transport
- Access to Fitness Passport – discounted gym memberships
- A supportive and inclusive work culture
- Bondi Junction office location close to Bondi Beach, Bronte and Tamarama!
- Opportunities for professional development and career progression
- Wellness that works for you! From annual skin checks and flu shots to our bi-annual health fair, we’re committed to helping you stay healthy
The Role
- To assist in the delivery of Civil Design projects for Major Projects, Infrastructure services and Integrated Transport,
 - Perform site inspections and assist in site surveys,
 - Assist with the preparation of project documentation including design drawings, estimates of cost, reports and calculations,
 - Contribute to ensuring work is completed on schedule and within budget, and
 - General project administration.
 About You
- Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering or associated discipline (if applying as Graduate Engineer) or in the process of obtaining tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering or associated discipline (if applying as Cadet Engineer).
- Demonstrated good level of communication (verbal and written) and interpersonal skills.
- Knowledge in principles of design and construction of civil and drainage works, knowledge in surveying including use of Total Station.
- Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel and Project along with good level of communication and interpersonal skills
- Current NSW Driver’s Licence
- Strong commitment to liaising with the client and team members.
 - A proactive attitude and willingness to learn.
 Please refer to the position description for detailed information on the position and required skills and experience. For more information contact Alice McCosker, Senior Design Engineer, alice.mccosker@waverley.nsw.gov.au
How to apply?
To be considered for this role, you will need to complete the following:
- A cover letter outlining your motivation for the role
 - A current resume detailing your relevant experience
 - Complete the online questionnaire demonstrating how you meet each of the essential criteria
 - All applications must be submitted through the Council’s website. waverley.nsw.gov.au/council/jobs
 Please note that pre-employment checks are part of the recruitment process. Depending on the volume and suitability of applications received, the vacancy may close prior to the advertised closing date. Shortlisting and interviewing may commence prior to the closing date. Early applications are therefore encouraged.
About Waverley Council
At Waverley Council, our values of Respect, Integrity, Innovation, Collaboration and Care guide how we work together, deliver, lead and support our community.
We are committed to providing an accessible and inclusive recruitment process. If you require adjustments or support at any stage, please contact our People and Culture team at recruitment@waverley.nsw.gov.au.
Waverley Council is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all candidates. We value diversity. We encourage applications from people from diverse groups, including, but not limited to, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island people; people from culturally diverse backgrounds; young people; older workers; people with disabilities; LGBTQIA+; and other minority groups.
We fully support the aims and objectives of the NSW Officer of Children's Guardian and Child Protection legislation. We will implement necessary practices to ensure a safe and supported Council environment for children and
How to apply: Visit waverley.nsw.gov.au/council/jobs
Applications close: 10 October 2026

candidates.title: Graduate Engineer
candidates.abstract: Graduate Engineer to join experienced civil crew completing flood restoration works throughout South East Queensland and Northern New South Wales.
bullets: Gain experience working under an experienced team.
Accommodation and Living Away from Home Allowance (LAHA) provided.
Accelerate your career with hands-on site experience.
screening_questions: Do you own or have regular access to a car?
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
Do you have experience using Microsoft Excel?
Do you hold a Construction Induction Safety certificate (White Card)?
Have you worked in a role which requires a sound understanding of OH&S/WHS?
How much notice are you required to give your current employer?
Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
Are you willing to relocate for this role?
candidates.content_text:
We are currently undertaking slope stabilisation works throughout South East Queensland and Northern New South Wales for various local and state government entities. 
For this job role, you will be expected to complete following daily tasks:
- Generating and completing Inspection and Test Plans (ITPS).
- Creating lots and logging data in to quality assurance system.
- Collecting and recording plant and labour dockets in excel.
- Material procurement. 
- Reporting to site engineer/ project engineer.
A central shared site house will be provided, but candidate will be expected to provide their own transport to site. 
You will be supported by an experienced crew who will be able to guide you as you develop your skills in the industry.
Works include; soil nails installation, micro-piles, bored piles, rock fall retention netting, rock fall retention fencing, retaining walls.

candidates.title: 2027 Graduate Program - Engineering
candidates.abstract: Join UrbanGrad 2027 and help solve complex engineering challenges that support essential services, sustainability and thriving SEQ communities
bullets: This is more than a program, it's a career pathway into the world of water
Work at the intersection of engineering, networks and infrastructure investment
WFH on offer, WORK180 endorsed employer for women, 97k/year + Super
candidates.content_text:
APPLICATIONS ARE OPEN FOR URBANGRAD 2027
Discover a career in water through our UrbanGrad Program. This is more than a program, it's a career pathway.
At Urban Utilities, we deliver essential water and wastewater services that support the health, liveability and sustainability of communities across South East Queensland. Through the UrbanGrad Program, you'll help shape the future of an industry that every person and every community depends on.
We're excited to open applications for the 2027 UrbanGrad Program, commencing in January 2027.
About UrbanGrad
UrbanGrad is more than a graduate program. It's the beginning of a long-term career at Urban Utilities.
Our newly designed 12-month graduate program combines meaningful work, rotational experiences, dedicated mentoring and structured development, with an assured ongoing permanent role upon successful completion.
From day one, you'll contribute to projects that make a genuine impact on our customers, communities and environment while developing the skills, confidence and networks to build a rewarding career in the water industry.
Engineering Disciplines
We welcome graduates with the following degrees and backgrounds:
- Process Engineering
- Chemical Engineering
​What you will be doing as an UrbanGrad
As a Process/Chemical Engineering UrbanGrad, you'll gain exposure to a variety of engineering environments across the business, including wastewater treatment, water supply networks, infrastructure delivery and specialist engineering teams. Through rotational experiences, you'll work alongside engineers, operators and project teams to understand how essential water and wastewater services are delivered, maintained and improved across Southeast Queensland.
You'll contribute to projects that support operational performance, environmental sustainability and public health, while building capability in process optimisation, asset management and infrastructure investment. From treatment plants and supply networks to strategic projects and specialist engineering functions, you'll develop a broad understanding of the critical role engineering plays in delivering essential services to our customers and communities.
We're looking for people who are:
- Influencers and innovators who display tenacity and are willing to challenge the status quo. 
- Sustainability-minded individuals who are committed to a greener future for our customers and communities.
- Self-starters who bring their enthusiasm and growth mindset to achieve amazing outcomes. 
- Natural collaborators who enjoy building meaningful relationships and working with others to achieve customer-centric outcomes.
- Digitally savvy and skilled problem solvers who are curious to learn from others. 
Why join UrbanGrad?
- Start your career with confidence with an assured ongoing role upon successful completion of a 12-month graduate program.
- Leading remuneration of $97,000/year + Super. This will increase from July 1st 2027, per the Enterprise Agreement.
- Join a Prosple Top 100 Graduate Employer, offering a flexible workplace, inclusive culture and a friendly, transparent recruitment experience.
- Work on projects that matter, tackling complex engineering challenges related to infrastructure development, climate resilience, environmental sustainability and the future needs of South East Queensland communities.
- Be supported to thrive. We're proud to be a WORK180 Endorsed Employer and accredited Australian Workplace Equality Index Employer, creating opportunities for emerging talent to succeed and grow.
- Learn from the best. Benefit from a structured program including a dedicated program mentor, rotational experiences aligned to your discipline, learning and development opportunities, and exposure to leaders and subject matter experts across the business.
- Be part of an organisation committed to meaningful impact, including strengthening our relationships with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples through our Reconciliation Action Plan.
Eligibility 
To be eligible, you must:
- Have completed, or be completing, a relevant degree within 24 months of the program commencement date of January 2027
- Be an Australian or New Zealand Citizen or have unrestricted working rights.
At UU, our strength comes from our people. We value different perspectives, backgrounds, experiences and ways of thinking, and we're committed to creating a workplace where people feel respected, included, and supported to do their best work. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities and life experiences.
You do not need to meet every requirement to apply. If this role interests you and you feel you could contribute, we'd love to hear from you. 
If you require adjustments at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know. We're here to support you through the process. 
Recruitment timelines: 
- September/October: applications are open from 7th September - 11th October
- October: shortlisting and phone interviews with the Talent Team
- November: in-person "Grad Day" at our head office in Fortitude Valley
- November: offers to join the UrbanGrad Program 
- January 2027: start with Urban Utilities
How to apply
Click 'Apply' and follow the prompts. Applications will take no more than 10 minutes.
Applications close at 11:59pm on Sunday October 11th.
For further information, please contact our Talent Team at careers@urbanutilities.com.au
Please note: Successful applicants will be required to complete pre-employment checks as part of the recruitment process.

candidates.title: Cadet - Civil Engineering
candidates.abstract: Gain hands-on civil engineering experience, paid study support and mentoring while helping deliver projects that shape our city.
candidates.location: Shellharbour, Wollongong, Illawarra & South Coast NSW
bullets: Paid cadetship with mentoring and professional support
Exposure to roads, drainage and civil construction
Apply university learning to real community projects
candidates.content_text:
Are you currently studying a Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) and looking to gain real-world engineering experience while you complete your degree?
Launch your engineering career with Shellharbour City Council and develop practical skills, industry knowledge and professional networks through a structured cadetship program designed to support your transition from university to the workplace.
The Civil Engineer Cadetship is a structured training and development opportunity for students who have successfully completed at least four semesters (96 credit points) of a Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) and are about to commence or are currently undertaking their third year of study.
Combining paid practical experience with ongoing study, you'll work alongside experienced engineers and professionals across Engineering, Asset Strategy and our Oak Flats Services Depot, gaining valuable exposure to a broad range of local government engineering functions.
You will have the opportunity to contribute to projects that shape the future of one of NSW's fastest growing cities. 
Gain hands-on experience across areas such as:
 - Road and transport infrastructure
 - Traffic engineering
 - Flood and stormwater management
 - Civil works and construction projects
 - Project delivery and asset planning and management
 This is an opportunity to apply what you're learning at university to real projects that make a difference in the local community.
Through Council's Cadet, Apprentice and Trainee (CAT) Program, you'll receive ongoing mentoring, professional development and on-the-job training while completing your degree. The program is designed to build future talent and support students to develop the technical, professional and leadership skills needed for a successful career.
For more information on our CAT Program, click here.
About us: 
Shellharbour City, located in the Illawarra region, is just 80 minutes south of Sydney and is home to over 86,000 people in a city that spans 154 square kilometres. It's an area of great natural beauty - stretching west from the picturesque coastline to rolling pastures, set against the majestic backdrop of the Illawarra escarpment. 
Our dedication to be financially sustainable in an evolving environment, while striving for a great organisational culture and committing to employing staff who embrace our core values, has made Shellharbour City Council an employer of choice.
We have been recognised with numerous state and national awards in recent times, including eight wins for our First Nations Community the Yirran Muru (many pathways) playspace, as well as being presented as winners in the NSW Landscape Architecture Awards, Regional Achievement Awards, and Parks and Leisure Australia Regional Awards of Excellence.
We offer:
Shellharbour City Council offers a high performing and sustainable organisation to deliver outcomes for the community through leadership, collaboration and innovation. We have exciting, rewarding career opportunities and flexible working arrangements to support a healthy work/life balance. 
 - Temporary full time, 35 hours per week with access to flexi-time 
 - Commencing salary range from $1,116.30 - $1,279.60 per week (based on university progression)
 - Plus 12% superannuation
 - Payment of course fees upon receipt of enrolment record
 - Additional Allowance of $230 per subject for essential student expenses such as administration fees, course materials including textbooks and prescribed readings
 - Study and Examination Leave for face-to-face and online courses
 - Structured Cadetship Program including a Mentor and Peer Program
 - Plus benefits including novated leasing, retail discounts, corporate fitness programs, Employee Assistance Program (EAP) support & Learning & Development opportunities
 - Plus Annual Award Increases & Bi-annual bonus payments & weekly pay run
 - Plus a range of local government benefits, including LSL after 5 years, one week 'My Leave', health & wellbeing initiatives as well as generous parental leave entitlements. 
 For further information about the position, click here for the position description.
Contact: Kristi Barrett, Team Leader Learning and Development on 4221 6236. 
Closing date: Monday, 5 October 2026 at 11:30pm. 
Apply now...
Complete the application below by answering the questions, describing how your skills and experience are relevant to the position. 
Your Resume and qualifications can be attached on the NEXT page.
Once you start your online application, you may save and return to this later, however incomplete applications will not be considered. You may wish to prepare your responses in a word document and then COPY and PASTE into the fields below. Your Resume and qualifications can be attached on the NEXT page.
When you have submitted your application, an email confirmation will be sent to your nominated email address. Please ensure you have the correct email address and check your inbox (including your "junk" inbox). 
For further information about the selection process including tips on how to address the selection criteria, please view our Guide to Applying. 
Shellharbour City Council is an Equal Opportunity Employer and values the unique strengths and talents of all people. Aboriginal Torres Strait Islander people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds and people with a disability are encouraged to apply.
At Shellharbour City Council we promote respect at work as a fundamental right for all and strive to create a workplace free from discrimination and harassment. This commitment extends to the promotion of the rights of all children and young people to be safe from harm when interacting with our services and spaces. Our values, Collaboration, Accountability, Integrity, Respect and Sustainability underpin all we do.
Your decision to apply for a role at Shellharbour City Council is the first step in acknowledging your alignment to our values and aspirations to create a great workplace.

candidates.title: Junior Draftsman
candidates.abstract: Fast paced role with exciting opportunities to work on a variety of different projects from small to large.
screening_questions: Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a draftsperson?
Which of the following CAD software do you have experience with?
How many years' experience do you have in the construction industry?
Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
candidates.content_text:
About Us
Launched in 2003, Cosmo Cranes is an Australian family owned & operated group that has earned a strong reputation as a leader of a reliable and modern crane fleet.
The group is made up of 5 divisions that all work in conjunction to provide a comprehensive range of materials handling solutions across a range of industrial, multi-story & high-rise construction projects.
The Role
An opportunity has become available for a Junior Draftsman. You will need great organisational & communication skills, be able to adapt to changes quickly, work well under pressure and help to maintain & continue to build upon the excellence of our team.
Key Requirements
-  Have Experience in AutoCAD
- Should have good familiarity with common AutoCAD commands. 
- Can work in model space & paper space.
- Can scale & import objects.
- Can use & modify blocks (& dynamic blocks – better).
- Familiarity of 3D Cartesian Space
- Cosmo draw 99% in 2D, but the candidate must understand how drawn items relate to the 3D world around it. 
- Current technical & engineering literacy
- Have a general understanding of how cranes move or work.
- Have a general understanding of building construction & engineering.
- Ability to learn new drafting concepts & techniques that may be unorthodox.
- The short term goal is to assimilate oneself to the current Cosmo drafting model.
Skills & Attributes
- Ability to work under pressure.
- Can work on multiple projects at any given time.
- Should have good time management & meet KPIs. 
- Self-motivated.
- Should have a strong passion & drive for the job.
- Self Confidence.
- Ability to show initiative. 
- Excellent communication skills – written & verbal
Full training will be provided along with support from the Drafting Team for the right candidate.
